record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: Extend the classification of semitoric systems F = (J, H) in [185, 186] to allow for F having non-degenerate singularities with hyperbolic bloc ks (a version of this problem was mentioned in various forms in [188]). The first step in this direction is in Dullin et al [70], see also a general approach to the symplectic classification problem in Zung [238]. Note that, in contrast with the semitoric case, even the topology o f a small neighbourhood of a singular fiber can be quite complicated, see e.g. [23, 37, 121, 151, 158, 159, 160, 183, 236, 237, 238]. There are also a number of interesting problems at the intersection of integrable systems and Hamil- tonian compact group actions, the following being one of them.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a connected symplectic $4$-manifold, and let $F=(J,H):M\to\mathbb{R}^2$ be a completely integrable Hamiltonian system, i.e. a smooth map whose components Poisson-commute and are functionally independent almost everywhere. Recall that a singular point $p\in M$ of $F$ is non-degenerate (in the Williamson sense) if the linearizations $dJ_p$, $dH_p$ generate a Cartan subalgebra of the Lie algebra $\mathrm{sp}(T_pM,\omega_p)$; in dimension four such a subalgebra decomposes as a direct sum of blocks of four possible types: elliptic, hyperbolic, focus–focus, and (in the corank-one case) regular.

A semitoric system is such an $F=(J,H)$ in which $J$ is proper and generates an effective Hamiltonian $S^1$-action, all singular points are non-degenerate, and no singular point has a hyperbolic block. Semitoric systems have been classified up to isomorphism by a list of symplectic invariants (number of focus–focus points, the Taylor-series invariant at each focus–focus point, the polygon invariant, the height invariant, and the twisting-index invariant).

Problem. Extend this classification to the class of integrable systems $F=(J,H)$ on $4$-dimensional symplectic manifolds for which $J$ still generates a proper Hamiltonian $S^1$-action and all singularities are non-degenerate, but where singular points with hyperbolic blocks are allowed. More precisely: produce a complete list of symplectic invariants, together with a realization theorem, classifying such systems up to isomorphism (where two systems $F_1$, $F_2$ are isomorphic if there exists a symplectomorphism $\varphi$ with $\varphi^*J_2=J_1$ and $\varphi^*H_2=f(J_1,H_1)$ for some smooth function $f$ with $\partial f/\partial H_1>0$).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of extending the Pelayo–Vũ Ngọc semitoric classification to allow hyperbolic blocks is the subject of active recent research. Hohloch and Palmer introduced "hypersemitoric systems" as a natural framework, and recent preprints (e.g. "Towards hypersemitoric systems", 2023, and "On the affine invariant of simple hypersemitoric systems", 2024) develop partial invariants (polygon/affine invariants, treatments of parabolic and transversally-hyperbolic singularities, Hopf-bifurcation constructions). A complete symplectic classification analogous to the semitoric case is not yet established, so the problem appears partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Towards hypersemitoric systems
status_evidence.snippet: Hypersemitoric systems are a natural generalization of semitoric systems... introduced by Hohloch and Palmer.
status_evidence.claim: A generalized class allowing hyperbolic-type singularities has been defined and is being studied, but full classification is in progress.

status_evidence.title: On the affine invariant of simple hypersemitoric systems
status_evidence.snippet: Affine invariant of simple hypersemitoric systems.
status_evidence.claim: Partial invariants extending the semitoric polygon to systems with hyperbolic singularities have been constructed.

status_evidence.title: Generating Hyperbolic Singularities in Semitoric Systems Via Hopf Bifurcations
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of integrable systems with transversally hyperbolic singular values via Hopf bifurcations from focus–focus.
status_evidence.claim: Construction techniques producing hyperbolic singularities in this setting exist (Dullin et al.).
